en.name: Sweet potato leaves
en.summary: Sweet potato leaves are the young shoot tips and leaves of the sweet potato vine, stir-fried with garlic or blanched and dressed. No figure is published for them, so treat them like spinach and shorten it: about 2–4 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: Sweet potato tips have no useful room-temperature life. They are soft new growth, thin-leaved and full of water, and in a warm kitchen a bundle wilts within a couple of hours and the cut stems start to brown. There is no pantry figure here and none should be assumed. Get them home and into the crisper, and cook them the day after you buy them at the latest.
en.fridge: Do not wash them, bag them loosely, and keep them in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. About 2–4 days is the working limit. The published figure for spinach is 3–5 days, and the range here is shortened from that because these tender shoot tips wilt noticeably faster than spinach does — nothing is published for sweet potato leaves themselves. Keep the bundle dry and uncrushed; water on the leaves and pressure from anything stacked on top are the two things that finish them.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for sweet potato leaves and freezing them is not worth doing. The appeal is a fresh, slightly slippery tenderness that comes out of a hot wok in under a minute, and freezing bursts the thin leaves so that what thaws is a dark green mass. Nothing unsafe happens, but nothing usable comes out. Buy a bundle you will cook that day; they are cheap enough that stockpiling is not the point.
spoilage: Leaves gone slimy, translucent or blackened at the edges
Yellowing leaves, or stems that have gone soft and bendy
Cut stem ends turned brown and dry
A sour or fermented smell when the bag is opened
tips: Choose bundles with springy leaves, firm stems and freshly cut, pale ends.
Do not wash before storing; bag them loosely and keep them dry.
Pick the tender tips off and discard any stem that bends instead of snapping.
Stir-fry hot and fast with garlic, or blanch briefly and dress — either way, under a minute.

faq.q: How long do sweet potato leaves last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 2–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, unwashed and loosely bagged. The published spinach figure is 3–5 days and this range is shortened from it, because these tips wilt faster.

faq.q: Can you freeze sweet potato leaves?
faq.a: There is no timeline and no point. The thin leaves collapse into a dark mass on thawing.
Yes, they are a staple green across Asia and the Pacific, and they are eaten cooked rather than raw. The leaves and tender tips are used; the tough lower stems are discarded.

faq.q: Why do the stems stay tough?
faq.a: Only the young tips are tender. Snap each stem at the point where it breaks cleanly — anything that bends instead of snapping will stay fibrous however long you cook it.

zh.name: 地瓜葉
zh.summary: 地瓜葉是番薯藤的嫩梢和幼葉，最常見的吃法是蒜炒或汆燙後拌醬。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照菠菜再往下縮短：4°C 以下冷藏約 2～4 天。
zh.pantry: 地瓜葉沒有什麼可用的常溫保存期。它是柔嫩的新生枝梢，葉薄又多水，在溫暖的廚房裡兩三個小時就萎了，莖的切口也會開始發褐。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請放進蔬果保鮮室，最晚隔天就要煮。
zh.fridge: 不清洗，鬆鬆裝袋放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，約 2～4 天是工作上限。菠菜公布的數字是 3～5 天，這裡往下縮短，是因為這種柔嫩的嫩梢萎得明顯比菠菜快——地瓜葉本身則沒有任何公布的數據。請保持整把乾燥、不要壓實；葉片上的水和上面堆疊的重量，就是終結它的兩件事。
zh.freezer: 地瓜葉沒有冷凍保存期限，冷凍也不值得。它的魅力在於那份清爽微滑的柔嫩，而那在熱鍋裡不到一分鐘就完成了；冷凍會撐破薄葉，解凍後只剩一團深綠色的東西。這不會有安全問題，但也沒有任何能用的東西。請買當天就會煮完的份量——它便宜到根本不需要囤。
spoilage: 葉片變黏、變得半透明，或葉緣發黑
葉子泛黃，或莖變得軟塌可彎
打開袋子聞到酸味或發酵味
tips: 挑葉片有彈性、莖結實、切口新鮮淡色的。
保存前不要洗；鬆鬆裝袋、保持乾燥。
把嫩梢摘下來用，折起來只會彎不會斷的莖就丟掉。
大火蒜炒，或快速汆燙後拌醬——兩種做法都在一分鐘以內。

faq.q: 地瓜葉放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、不清洗鬆鬆裝袋，約 2～4 天。菠菜公布的數字是 3～5 天，這裡往下縮短，因為嫩梢萎得更快。
沒有對應的期限，也沒有意義。薄葉解凍後會塌成一團深色的東西。
可以，它在亞洲和太平洋地區都是常見的家常青菜，一律煮熟吃而不生食。吃的是葉片和嫩梢，粗老的下段莖要丟掉。
只有嫩梢是軟的。請把每根莖從能乾脆折斷的地方折開——折起來只會彎的部分，不管煮多久都還是粗纖維。
